//: English, the base language, and the model for the others: every language defines each id of each table below. scripts/gen-i18n.py turns these files into the tables the app loads (resources/i18n/<lang>.xml) and their keys (source/I18nKeys.mc): run it after any change. Keys that start with // are notes, which it skips.
// templates: A template's $1$, $2$ are filled in by the app (Lang.format). A translation may reorder them or leave one out, as French PrayerNumber does, but never add one. Every text must fit the screen: LayoutTests.mc measures each one in its place.

glance.//: The glance: the day's mysteries over today's progress ("Joyful" over "Mystery 2/5"). It is the only table the glance can load, so it holds nothing else: each text here takes room in the glance's 32KB (scripts/check-glance-strings.py checks that the glance uses every one, and nothing else). PrayerSalve is the prayer the main screen names too.
glance.// GlanceInProgress: From the Creed to the first Glory Be.
glance.// GlanceMystery: $1$ the current mystery (1..5), $2$ how many there are (5).

ui.//: The full-screen widget's main screen, menu and reset prompt.
ui.// PrayerCreed: The prayers, as the main screen names the current bead in large type (a smaller font when a name is too wide for it).
ui.// PrayerNumber: A Hail Mary and its number in the decade: $1$ PrayerHailMary, $2$ the number (Hail Mary 7).
ui.// OpeningTitle: Title of the main screen at the opening and at the Salve.
ui.// SetTitleJoyful: Line under the title at the opening and at the Salve: the day's mysteries. Each set's title is a text of its own, not a template over the set's name, so each language writes it its own way (French "Mystères joyeux", the adjective in lower case).
ui.// MysteryTitle: Title of each mystery on the main screen, the menu and the reading view: $1$ the ordinal, $2$ the set's name in singular (1st Joyful Mystery).
ui.// MenuRead: Menu on hold UP, drawn by the app in the large font: short enough to fit on one line.

mysteries.//: The name of each mystery, under its title on the main screen and first in the reading view. MysteryN follows Rosary.mysteryIndex + 1, like QuoteN and RefN: Joyful 1..5, Sorrowful 6..10, Glorious 11..15, Luminous 16..20. Each name fits 2 lines on the main screen.
mysteries.Mystery13: The Descent of the Holy Spirit
mysteries.Mystery16: The Baptism of Christ in the Jordan
mysteries.Mystery18: The Proclamation of the Kingdom of God

// quotes: A Bible quote for each mystery and its reference, read from the menu on hold UP ("Read mystery"). One table per set, so the reading view loads only its own set's. QuoteN and RefN follow Rosary.mysteryIndex + 1: Joyful 1..5, Sorrowful 6..10, Glorious 11..15, Luminous 16..20. Source: the Douay-Rheims Bible, Challoner revision (public domain), as published at https://www.drbo.org/; one URL per quote in odd/tasks/rosary-distribution.md. Each quote is copied verbatim from the verse text there, and the references use its numbering (Mark 9 follows the Vulgate: the voice from the cloud is verse 6). "…" marks an excerpt that starts or ends inside a sentence.

quotesJoyful.Quote1: And the angel being come in, said unto her: Hail, full of grace, the Lord is with thee: blessed art thou among women.
quotesJoyful.Quote2: Blessed art thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb.
quotesJoyful.Quote3: And she brought forth her firstborn son, and wrapped him up in swaddling clothes, and laid him in a manger…
quotesJoyful.Quote4: …my eyes have seen thy salvation, Which thou hast prepared before the face of all peoples…
quotesJoyful.Quote5: And he said to them: How is it that you sought me? did you not know, that I must be about my father's business?

quotesSorrowful.Quote6: Father, if thou wilt, remove this chalice from me: but yet not my will, but thine be done.
quotesSorrowful.Quote7: Then therefore, Pilate took Jesus, and scourged him.
quotesSorrowful.Quote8: And the soldiers platting a crown of thorns, put it upon his head; and they put on him a purple garment.
quotesSorrowful.Quote9: And bearing his own cross, he went forth to that place which is called Calvary, but in Hebrew Golgotha.
quotesSorrowful.Quote10: And Jesus crying out with a loud voice, said: Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit. And saying this, he gave up the ghost.

quotesGlorious.Quote11: Why seek you the living with the dead? He is not here, but is risen.
quotesGlorious.Quote12: And when he had said these things, while they looked on, he was raised up: and a cloud received him out of their sight.
quotesGlorious.Quote13: …And they were all filled with the Holy Ghost, and they began to speak with divers tongues, according as the Holy Ghost gave them to speak.
quotesGlorious.Quote14: Because he hath regarded the humility of his handmaid; for behold from henceforth all generations shall call me blessed.
quotesGlorious.Quote15: And a great sign appeared in heaven: A woman clothed with the sun, and the moon under her feet, and on her head a crown of twelve stars…

quotesLuminous.Quote16: And behold a voice from heaven, saying: This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.
quotesLuminous.Quote17: His mother saith to the waiters: Whatsoever he shall say to you, do ye.
quotesLuminous.Quote18: The time is accomplished, and the kingdom of God is at hand: repent, and believe the gospel.
quotesLuminous.Quote19: And there was a cloud overshadowing them: and a voice came out of the cloud, saying: This is my most beloved son; hear ye him.
quotesLuminous.Quote20: This is my body, which is given for you. Do this for a commemoration of me.
